blockers.description: flutter build apk --release fails by design when android/key.properties is absent, with an explicit message rather than a silent fallback to the debug signing config.
blockers.workaround: Intended behaviour, not a defect. A release build signed with a debug key is a failure that only surfaces after upload. Resolve by creating the keystore, never by relaxing the Gradle check.

decisions.decision: D-33 amended a second time, from 7+1 to 7+3 (P6-D-26), admitting GarageScreen and ItemManagementScreen as pushed Scaffold screens.
decisions.rationale: User chose amend-7-plus-3 at 06-05's opening checkpoint. Both screens are reachable only from Settings, add no top-level navigation point, and are Settings-internal CRUD — the same class of exception Phase 3 named for DataIssueScreen. The alternative (bottom sheets) was rejected by 06-UI-SPEC.md on usability: no independent app bar, and keyboard avoidance at row depth for two numeric fields degrades worst on the 3-4 GB target device. Recorded in PROJECT.md with 'none of them a precedent for a fourth'.

decisions.decision: The missing odoReminderDayOfMonth Settings control was built immediately, out of plan, rather than waived or deferred to a gap plan.
decisions.rationale: User chose this at the 06-07 precondition checkpoint. It made 06-07's precondition hold genuinely instead of being waived, and stopped SET-02 from failing at end-of-phase verification. The field already existed in the model with @Default(1) // 1-28 and was already consumed by the notification planner; only the UI row was missing. Built as a bounded 28-item radio selector so an out-of-range value is unrepresentable by construction, matching the leadDays row's own guarantee.

decisions.decision: Ten pre-existing dart-format-drifted files from Phases 1/2/5 were reformatted in a standalone commit (3a34c01) between waves 2 and 3.
decisions.rationale: Not tidying. CLAUDE.md instructs every executor to run `dart format .` before committing, so the drift would have been swept into whichever unrelated Phase 6 plan committed next, polluting its scope and risking add/add collisions between parallel worktree agents. Doing it once, on main, between waves, removed the hazard. backup_timing.dart:56 additionally needed braces because the formatter split a single-statement if whose trailing comment exceeded 80 chars, which then tripped curly_braces_in_flow_control_structures.

decisions.decision: Settled checkpoints were resolved inside the dispatch prompt via a <checkpoint_resolution> block instead of letting the executor halt.
decisions.rationale: 06-07's plan names the project's own recorded anti-pattern: a checkpoint whose answer was already in CONTEXT once burned ~147K tokens producing nothing. P6-D-11 (Drive checkbox opt-in, unchecked) and P6-D-12 (two-step dialog, concrete counts, no type-to-confirm) were already settled in 06-CONTEXT.md, so the dispatch carried the stance and asked only for the copy, recorded in the SUMMARY for later review. This worked — the executor did not re-ask.

decisions.decision: Neither the keystore nor the push was performed by an agent.
decisions.rationale: A keystore holds a private key that must stay with the user and whose passwords must never enter an agent transcript. Pushing ~390 commits to a public GitHub repo is an outward-facing action the user did not request. Both were reported as user actions with exact commands instead.
